title: QuTech Spinout Q*Bird Rebrands to Falqon Systems to Commercialize Quantum Secure Networks - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Delft QuTech/TU Delft spinout Q*Bird renamed itself Falqon Systems to mark a shift from QKD hardware components to end-to-end Quantum Secure Networks, keeping ownership, CEO Ingrid Romijn, contracts and roadmap intact. Its MDI-QKD architecture uses an untrusted central detector hub to kill detector side-channel attacks and enable star topologies, and it already runs deployments in six European countries including Madrid's MadQCI, aligned with EuroQCI sovereignty goals.

insights.claim: Delft-based quantum communications developer Q*Bird has officially transitioned into Falqon Systems, adopting a unified corporate identity while ownership structure, leadership under CEO Dr. Ingrid Romijn, existing customer contracts and technology roadmaps all remain unchanged.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A pure identity change with no cap-table or contract disruption means continuity of revenue and no hidden distress signal behind the rename.
insights.quote: the company’s ownership structure, leadership team under CEO Dr. Ingrid Romijn, existing customer contracts, and technological roadmaps remain unchanged

insights.claim: The company originated as a spinout from QuTech and Delft University of Technology in 2022, placing it roughly four years from lab spinout to multi-country commercial deployments.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A four-year lab-to-deployment cycle is a useful benchmark for how fast European quantum-communications spinouts can reach revenue-bearing networks.
insights.quote: Originating as a spinout from QuTech and Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) in 2022

insights.claim: The rebrand marks a strategic shift from selling hardware components to deploying end-to-end Quantum Secure Networks, consolidating hardware devices, key lifecycle management and network orchestration software under one platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Moving from component vendor to full-stack platform raises deal size and stickiness but also raises the capital and integration burden.
insights.quote: to support its expansion from hardware component manufacturing to deploying end-to-end Quantum Secure Networks (QSN)

insights.claim: The core architecture is built on Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution, which routes quantum signals through a central untrusted hub and thereby eliminates detector-side channel attack vectors present in traditional point-to-point QKD.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removing trust from the central node is the argument that lets QKD vendors sell into networks where a trusted-node model would be rejected outright.
insights.quote: routes quantum signals through a central untrusted hub, eliminating detector-side channel attack vectors

insights.claim: MDI-QKD allows multi-node star topologies where many parties share cryptographic keys without exposing raw keys at the central junction, a topology advantage over point-to-point links.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Topology economics decide QKD unit costs: one shared detector hub serving many spokes is far cheaper per endpoint than pairwise links.
insights.quote: allowing multi-node star topologies to share cryptographic keys without exposing raw keys at the central junction

insights.claim: The Falqon Key Manager handles hybrid key lifecycle management that integrates QKD with post-quantum cryptography and exposes an ETSI GS QKD 014 compliance interface.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Combining QKD with PQC rather than positioning them as rivals is how QKD vendors stay relevant as software-only PQC becomes the default.

insights.claim: The Falqon Domain Controller applies software-defined networking control for dynamic optical routing, key allocation and cross-domain orchestration across multi-site quantum networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Orchestration software is the recurring-revenue layer of a quantum network business, where hardware alone would be a one-time sale.

insights.claim: Falqon Systems maintains operational deployments across six countries — the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, Austria and Spain — including the Madrid Quantum Communication Infrastructure network run with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Six live national deployments is a real reference base, distinguishing this from QKD vendors still running single pilot links.
insights.quote: operational deployments across the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, Austria, and Spain

insights.claim: Engineering and manufacturing the platform in Europe aligns it with European digital sovereignty objectives under the European Quantum Communication Infrastructure initiative, positioning EuroQCI national backbones as a named deployment target.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: EU-made supply chain is effectively a procurement qualification for EuroQCI budgets, giving European vendors a protected demand pool.
insights.quote: Engineered and manufactured in Europe, the platform aligns with European digital sovereignty objectives

insights.claim: Target deployment environments span metropolitan telecom and fiber links, data center interconnects, government and defense networks, financial routing networks, sovereign cloud infrastructure and critical energy grids.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The named verticals are all regulated, long-sales-cycle buyers, which implies lumpy but defensible revenue.

insights.claim: The underlying MDI-QKD network architecture is designed to scale beyond cryptographic key exchange toward long-term quantum internet applications including quantum interconnects, distributed quantum computing and networked quantum sensors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If the same deployed fiber and hub hardware can later carry distributed quantum computing traffic, today's QKD contracts buy an option on a much larger market.
insights.quote: designed to scale beyond cryptographic key exchange to support long-term quantum internet applications
